title: Volume & Surface Area
sub: How much fits inside vs. how much wrapping paper

steps.html:
Volume & Surface Area

Volume = l × w × h8 × 3 × 6 = 144 cubic units: how much fits inside
Surface areaadd the 6 faces: the wrapping paper
say: Today: boxes. Two questions: how much fits inside, and how much wrapping paper covers the outside.
Volume is how much fits inside: length times width times height. Eight times three times six, one forty-four cubic units.
Surface area is the wrapping paper: the total area of all six faces.

steps.html:
Surface area: faces come in pairs

front & back: 2 × (8 × 6) = 96
top & bottom: 2 × (8 × 3) = 48
two sides: 2 × (3 × 6) = 36
total = 180 square units
say: A box has six faces, in three matching pairs. Front and back, eight by six, two of them, ninety-six. Top and bottom, eight by three, forty-eight. The two sides, three by six, thirty-six.
Add them up: one eighty square units.

steps.html:
Cubes and cylinders

cubeV = side3. Edge 3 → 27
cylinderV = πr2 × h (circle area × height)
say: A cube has all edges equal, so its volume is the side cubed. Edge three gives twenty-seven. That's why it's called cubed!
A cylinder, like a can, is the circle's area times the height: pi r squared times h.

steps.html: A cylinder has radius 5 and height 2. What is its volume?
say: A cylinder has radius five and height two. What's its volume?
steps.okSay: Yes! Pi times twenty-five times two, fifty pi.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Pi times five squared times two: twenty-five times two is fifty, so fifty pi.

steps.html: A box's length, width, and height are all doubled. Its volume becomes…
say: A box's length, width, and height are all doubled. What happens to its volume?
steps.okSay: Yes! Two times two times two is eight times as big.
steps.no: Each of the three measurements doubles: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 times.
steps.noSay: Not quite. All three measurements double, so the volume grows two times two times two, eight times.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Volume = l × w × h, in cubic units.

2. Surface area = add all 6 faces (3 pairs).

3. Cube: side3. Cylinder: πr2h.

4. Double every side → volume × 8.
say: Let's review. Volume is length times width times height, in cubic units.
Surface area adds all six faces, which come in three pairs.
A cube is the side cubed, and a cylinder is pi r squared h.
Double every side and the volume grows eight times. Nice work!
